answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, weighting identities by independently supported paths rather than their raw number. A sybil cluster with few links to the honest graph has low conductance: few walks escape its boundary, limiting the influence it can relay. With capped per-source weight and sufficient honest connectivity, this bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. A spiral of copied attestations cannot create independent support; even ferrous links across a terrace of identities matter only when they cross the cut.
